title: Hash Browns
subtitle: Crispy shredded potato cakes
excerpt: Hash browns are shredded potatoes, squeezed dry, formed into flat cakes, and fried in butter and oil until crispy on both sides. The key to hash browns is removing as much moisture from the potato as possible before frying: wet potato steams rather than crisps.
sourceNotes: Hash browns (or hashed brown potatoes) are a staple of the American diner breakfast. The name derives from the French hacher (to chop or mince). They appeared in American cookbooks from the late 19th century and became a diner staple in the early 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Grate and squeeze the potato up to 1 hour ahead, keeping covered in the fridge.

content.text: Hash browns are almost always soggy because people skip the drying step. Grate the potato, then squeeze it in a clean tea towel as hard as possible. Then squeeze again. The drier the potato, the crispier the result. Use a starchy potato (Maris Piper, King Edward): waxy varieties do not crisp properly.

items.prepNote: starchy variety (Maris Piper), peeled and coarsely grated

content.text: Place the grated potato in the centre of a clean tea towel. Gather the edges and wring tightly to squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Open, turn the potato, and squeeze again.
Season the dried potato with salt and pepper. Divide into 4 equal portions and shape into flat rounds about 1 cm thick.

Heat the oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the butter is foaming. Add the hash browns and press down with a spatula. Cook undisturbed for 5 to 6 minutes until deeply golden on the underside. Flip and cook for a further 5 to 6 minutes. They should be dark golden and very crispy on both sides.

items.symptom: Hash browns are soft and soggy, not crispy
items.cause: Potato was not sufficiently dried before frying
items.fix: Squeeze the potato twice in a tea towel. The amount of water that comes out is remarkable. Dry potato = crispy result.

items.symptom: Hash brown falls apart when flipped
items.cause: Crust had not fully formed on the underside
items.fix: Wait until the hash brown releases easily from the pan before flipping. A firm golden crust holds it together.
